A quick check of some of my dictionaries reveals the following:

Irregardless was in the Websters Second New International, published in 1957, my oldest dictionary. There it is noted as humorous or erroneous.

It is in Websters Third New International, 1993 version, noted as nonstandard.

Random House, second edition unabridged, 1987, notes it is nonstandard, but includes a note that even educated speakers use it to add emphasis.

Oxford English Dictionary, Second Edition, 1991, has it as being chiefly a North American term used in nonstandard or humorous use.
